pages.title: Three properties of a score
pages.text:
Three properties of a score
Ranking concerns ordering, classiﬁcation concerns a threshold, and probability prediction
concerns numerical event probabilities.
Improving one need not improve all three.

pages.title: Freeze preprocessing
pages.text:
Freeze preprocessing
The training median, means and scales are reused for validation and testing.
The
missingness indicator records absence; it does not recover the missing information.

pages.text:
The Brier score

It evaluates probabilities, not only the chosen classiﬁcation threshold.

pages.text:
Conditional probability decomposition
E[(p − Y )2 | X] = ( p − η)2 + η(1 − η).
The minimum occurs at the true conditional event probability η.

pages.title: Reliability bins
pages.text:
Reliability bins
Each bin compares its mean forecast with its observed event fraction.
Counts determine
how much information each point contains; an empty bin has no empirical fraction.
Computational Cardiology Notes 15 / 19

pages.title: Remove B while retaining the same groups
pages.text:
Remove B while retaining the same groups
Replace B by the frozen missing-data rule and retain every test outcome.
The change
measures sensitivity to this particular information-loss intervention.

pages.title: AUC and probability quality can separate
pages.text:
AUC and probability quality can separate
Positive temperature leaves AUC unchanged while changing Brier score and likelihood.
A
better probability score on one sample is an empirical result, not an algebraic guarantee.
Computational Cardiology Notes 18 / 19
